import org.json.JSONArray
import org.json.JSONObject

/** 会话索引：当前会话 id + 全部会话元数据（消息本体在 {id}.json，见 ChatStore）。 */
data class SessionIndex(
    val currentId: String?,
    val sessions: List<ChatSession>,
)

/**
 * 会话索引 JSON 编解码（纯 Kotlin + org.json，JVM 可单测；文件 IO 在 ChatStore）。
 * 坏 JSON / 非对象 / 缺 sessions → 空索引（绝不因索引损坏崩 App；消息文件各自独立不受牵连）。
 */
object SessionIndexCodec {

    fun encode(index: SessionIndex): String {
        val arr = JSONArray()
        for (s in index.sessions) {
            arr.put(
                JSONObject()
                    .put("id", s.id)
                    .put("title", s.title)
                    .put("createdAt", s.createdAt)
                    .put("updatedAt", s.updatedAt)
                    .put("titleManual", s.titleManual),

            .put("current", index.currentId ?: JSONObject.NULL)
            .put("sessions", arr)
            .toString()
    }

        val arr = o.optJSONArray("sessions") ?: return SessionIndex(null, emptyList())

        for (i in 0 until arr.length()) {
            val s = arr.optJSONObject(i) ?: continue
            val id = s.optString("id", "")

                    createdAt = s.optLong("createdAt", 0L),

                    titleManual = s.optBoolean("titleManual", false),
                ),
            )
        }
        val current = o.optString("current", "").takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }
        return SessionIndex(current, sessions)
    }
}

package com.xiaoduo.deskpet.chat

import org.json.JSONArray
import org.json.JSONObject

/** 会话索引：当前会话 id + 全部会话元数据（消息本体在 {id}.json，见 ChatStore）。 */
data class SessionIndex(
    val currentId: String?,
    val sessions: List<ChatSession>,
)

/**
 * 会话索引 JSON 编解码（纯 Kotlin + org.json，JVM 可单测；文件 IO 在 ChatStore）。
 * 坏 JSON / 非对象 / 缺 sessions → 空索引（绝不因索引损坏崩 App；消息文件各自独立不受牵连）。
 */
object SessionIndexCodec {

    fun encode(index: SessionIndex): String {
        val arr = JSONArray()
        for (s in index.sessions) {
            arr.put(
                JSONObject()
                    .put("id", s.id)
                    .put("title", s.title)
                    .put("createdAt", s.createdAt)
                    .put("updatedAt", s.updatedAt)
                    .put("titleManual", s.titleManual),
            )
        }
        return JSONObject()
            .put("current", index.currentId ?: JSONObject.NULL)
            .put("sessions", arr)
            .toString()
    }

    fun decode(json: String): SessionIndex {
        val o = runCatching { JSONObject(json) }.getOrNull() ?: return SessionIndex(null, emptyList())
        val arr = o.optJSONArray("sessions") ?: return SessionIndex(null, emptyList())
        val sessions = ArrayList<ChatSession>(arr.length())
        for (i in 0 until arr.length()) {
            val s = arr.optJSONObject(i) ?: continue
            val id = s.optString("id", "")
            if (id.isBlank()) continue
            sessions.add(
                ChatSession(
                    id = id,
                    title = s.optString("title", ChatSession.FALLBACK_TITLE),
                    createdAt = s.optLong("createdAt", 0L),
                    updatedAt = s.optLong("updatedAt", 0L),
                    // 向后兼容：旧索引无此字段，缺省 false（继续走 deriveTitle）
                    titleManual = s.optBoolean("titleManual", false),
                ),
            )
        }
        val current = o.optString("current", "").takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }
        return SessionIndex(current, sessions)
    }
}

object ThinkCleaner {

    private val BLOCK = Regex("<think>[\\s\\S]*?</think>")
    private const val OPEN = "<think>"
    private const val CLOSE = "</think>"

    fun clean(raw: String): String {
        if (raw.isEmpty()) return raw
        var s = BLOCK.replace(raw, "")
        val open = s.indexOf("<think")
        if (open >= 0) s = s.substring(0, open)
        s = s.replace(CLOSE, "")
        s = dropTrailingPartial(s, CLOSE)
        s = dropTrailingPartial(s, OPEN)
        return s
    }

    private fun dropTrailingPartial(s: String, tag: String): String {
        val max = minOf(tag.length - 1, s.length)
        for (len in max downTo 1) {
            if (s.endsWith(tag.substring(0, len))) return s.dropLast(len)
        }
        return s
    }
}

comments.content: The check-then-act on done.count is not atomic. If a task-finished/onClosed countDown lands between the `done.count == 0L` check and the `error = ...` write, a late failure can flip an already-successful task into an error: the caller's await() has already returned, but it then reads a non-null `error` and discards the fully received audio. Note that `error` (and `pcm`) are plain captured vars mutated on OkHttp threads with no synchronization of their own — correctness currently relies solely on the latch's happens-before edge, which this interleaving breaks. Use an AtomicBoolean 'finished' set in the task-finished branch plus an AtomicReference for the error with compareAndSet, so a terminal state is decided exactly once.

comments.content: block.colMaxUnits is a computed getter in MarkdownRenderer (List(header.size) { ... maxOf { displayUnits(...) } }), i.e. it re-scans and re-measures every cell of the table on EACH access. This file accesses it once per cell — in the header AND in every body row — so a table with H columns and R rows triggers H*(R+1) full column-max recomputations (each allocating joined strings) per recomposition. In streaming chat the table is recomposed on every token, so this multiplies already O(rows*cols) parse work severely and can jank long tables. Hoist it once at the top of TableBlock (e.g. `val colUnits = remember(block) { block.colMaxUnits }`) and pass `colUnits` into both forEachIndexed sites.
comments.thinking:
Key findings from MarkdownRenderer:

1. `Block.Table` docs say "单元格数量对齐 header（多砍少补空）" — the parser normalizes rows to header width via `norm()`. So rows always have exactly `header.size` cells! This changes focus area #2: `getOrElse(idx) { 8 }` fallback would never trigger for rows shorter than header, since parser pads. But: `colMaxUnits` is a computed property with a getter (not stored!) — it recomputes the entire column-max computation **every time it's accessed** — and it's accessed twice per table render (header + each row!). Look:

```kotlin
val colMaxUnits: List<Int>
    get() = List(header.size) { idx -> ... maxOf { displayUnits(...) } }
```

In MarkdownContent.kt:
- Header row: `block.colMaxUnits.getOrElse(idx) { 8 }` — computed once per header cell → property getter invoked per cell!
- Each body row: `block.colMaxUnits.getOrElse(idx) { 8 }` — getter invoked per cell per row!

So for a table with H columns and R rows, `colMaxUnits` getter is invoked H + H*R times, each invocation doing O(H * R * cellLength) displayUnits computation. comments.content: Unbounded read before the size guard: readBytes() slurps the entire provider content into memory here, while the 20MB limit is only enforced later in vm.uploadFile. The picker uses "*/*", so users can select multi-hundred-MB videos/archives; the byte[] allocation can throw OutOfMemoryError, which the surrounding runCatching{}.getOrNull() then silently converts into the generic "读取文件失败" toast (it equally masks SecurityException and other failures as "read failed"). Suggest checking OpenableColumns.SIZE in the same cursor and rejecting oversized picks before reading, and/or streaming with a hard cap instead of readBytes().

Settings.canDrawOverlays() is a synchronous binder IPC call executed on the main thread inside the remember initializer during composition (and again on every ON_RESUME). The ON_RESUME path is fine because mutableStateOf's default structural-equality policy suppresses redundant recompositions, but the initial in-composition read couples UI composition to a system service call. Consider moving the initial check into a side effect (e.g. LaunchedEffect running once) or hoisting overlay state into a ViewModel so composition stays side-effect free.

comments.content: Unhandled exceptions in the search producer crash the whole composition: `onSearch(query)` runs inside `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` with no try/catch, so any I/O error thrown by the callback escapes the produceState producer coroutine and tears down the UI. Re-throw CancellationException (it must propagate for produceState to restart on key change) but catch other failures and degrade (log + empty/null). Two related issues in the same producer: (1) there is no debounce, so every keystroke schedules a disk search on Dispatchers.IO (prior runs are cancelled, but fast typing still thrashes IO — consider snapshotFlow + debounce ~250ms); (2) once the first search completes, `value` retains the previous result list while a re-search is in flight, so the '搜索中…' branch (which only fires when results == null) never shows again and stale results for the old query are displayed until the new one lands.

Dialog state is lost on configuration change / process death: `actionTarget`, `deleteCandidate` and `renameCandidate` use plain `remember`, so rotating the device silently closes any open action-menu/delete-confirm/rename dialog — inconsistent with `query` right above, which correctly uses `rememberSaveable`. ChatSession is not guaranteed Bundle-saveable, so persist the target session id (String?) instead of the object, and resolve the object from `sessions` when showing the dialogs.

comments.content: MAX_DRIFT_PX is a hard-coded pixel value whose "32px ≈ 5mm" rationale only holds at 1x density (as the doc itself states). Fix: wrap the entire run() body in one try/catch(Exception) that logs via PetLogger (and records backoff when key is available), instead of scattering per-call guards.

TOCTOU race between cache key and synthesized voice: key is derived from resolver.snapshot() at run() start, but ttsSynthesize(app, TEXT) leaves voice="default", so the actual timbre is read from live NetConfig inside CloudClientFactory at call time (per the class KDoc: "aliyun/volc 分支直接读 NetConfig"). Triggers arriving while a run is in flight are silently dropped: CAS fails and maybePrefetch returns without recording that work is owed. Since run() freezes the snapshot/cache key at start and synthesis+disk write can take seconds, a config saved during that window is never prefetched — the dropped caller's config stays uncached until the next unrelated trigger (session assembly or another save). The fallback chain masks it (vendor asset plays), but the "保存即合成 + 启动补漏" guarantee silently degrades. Fix: set a pending flag before the CAS-return and have the daemon re-check/re-run once at the end of run() with a fresh snapshot, so the latest saved config always gets prefetched.
